definition: Curvilinear regression is a form of regression analysis that examines relationships using model shapes such as quadratic, cubic, exponential, and logarithmic forms rather than relying only on a straight-line pattern. In the source, it is used to study and predict how one set of measurements relates to another when the relationship may be non-linear.
